summary.business_type: Local Service Area Business (Roofing Contractor) — Staten Island NY HQ, serving Brooklyn NY and 6 NJ towns

top_findings.title: Identical fake-looking review schema ("Product"/4.9★/97 reviews) duplicated verbatim on every single page, including FAQ and legal pages — a genuine spam-policy risk

5 orphan PPC landing pages (brooklyn-roofing-lp, roofer-old-bridge-nj, roofing-services-nj, affordable-roofing-in-brooklyn-ny, asphalt-shingle-roofing-staten-island) cannibalize the real /locations/ and /services/ pages — flagged independently by 6 of 11 audit categories
Sitewide RoofingContractor schema streetAddress field contains the business name ("ProLine Roofing") instead of a real street address — invalid NAP

Brooklyn and Freehold location pages assert specific street addresses in hidden JSON-LD (225 Joralemon St; 144 Tilton Dr) that appear nowhere in visible content — undisclosed-location / GBP policy risk

The primary market's own location page (/locations/staten-island-ny/) canonicalizes to the homepage and is missing from the sitemap, suppressing it from ranking independently for "Staten Island roofer" queries

quick_wins: Fix the "Saten Island" typo in the location page <title> tag
Add FAQPage schema to /faq/ and convert the accordion questions into real <h2>/<h3> headings
Publish an /llms.txt file summarizing the business, service area, and key pages
Fix the telePhone typo (should be telephone) in the Brooklyn location schema
Add explicit robots.txt Allow directives for GPTBot/OAI-SearchBot/ClaudeBot/PerplexityBot
Resolve the two different phone numbers shown on the same NJ location pages ((848) 310-3977 vs (347) 323-9128)

categories.name: Technical SEO
what_works: robots.txt is clean and correct (only /wp-admin/ disallowed) with a valid Sitemap pointer
Sitemap structure valid; all 4 sub-sitemaps well-formed and reachable
No broken pages or redirect chains found across 29 sampled URLs
Canonical tags present, correct, and self-referencing on every sampled page
Meta robots directives consistent (index, follow) — no accidental noindex
Non-www → www 301 redirect confirmed working
Universal mobile viewport tag; server-side rendered (not an SPA)

findings.title: Two orphan PPC landing pages are near-duplicate, thin, and indexable
findings.description: /roofer-old-bridge-nj/ and /roofing-services-nj/ extract to only 65–66 words of unique copy each, share a byte-identical meta description, are self-canonical, indexable, and sitemap-listed — directly cannibalizing /locations/new-jersey/old-bridge/.
findings.recommendation: Add noindex,follow or redirect to the real location/service page and drop from the sitemap.

findings.title: Zero security response headers site-wide
findings.description: None of 29 URLs checked returned HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, CSP, X-Frame-Options, or Referrer-Policy.
findings.recommendation: Add security headers via LiteSpeed config/.htaccess or a security-headers plugin; verify with securityheaders.com.

findings.title: Sitewide "Product" + fake review schema on every page type, including non-commercial pages
findings.description: Identical Product/AggregateRating (4.9/97) JSON-LD appears on FAQ, contact, legal, and location pages — misuse of structured data that risks suppression or a manual action.
findings.recommendation: Replace with LocalBusiness/RoofingContractor aggregateRating, scoped only to contextually appropriate pages.

findings.title: Local/multi-location structured data is inconsistent across location pages
findings.description: Only /locations/brooklyn-ny/ carries full RoofingContractor/GeoCoordinates/OpeningHours markup; the other 6+ location pages have none.
findings.recommendation: Apply the Brooklyn schema template to every location page, ideally via a dynamic Rank Math/Elementor module.

findings.title: 3 additional orphan PPC landing pages create duplicate-content/crawl-budget risk
findings.description: brooklyn-roofing-lp, affordable-roofing-in-brooklyn-ny, and asphalt-shingle-roofing-staten-island are indexable, self-canonical, sitemap-listed, and not linked from the homepage nav — ~10% of all sitemap entries are orphan PPC pages.
findings.recommendation: Noindex active ad destinations and drop from sitemap; 301 retired ones to the equivalent location/service page.

findings.title: Likely LCP-risk image-loading pattern and low modern-format adoption
findings.description: Hero/content images are JS-lazy-loaded via data-src even where fetchpriority="high" is set, defeating the preload hint; only ~6 of ~21 homepage images use WebP.
findings.recommendation: Exclude the true LCP image from lazy-load, keep it in initial HTML with fetchpriority="high", and expand WebP/AVIF adoption.

findings.title: Inconsistent location-page URL taxonomy
findings.description: NJ towns nest under /locations/new-jersey/, Brooklyn sits at /locations/brooklyn-ny/ with no NY parent, and Jersey City carries a redundant -nj suffix its siblings don't.
findings.recommendation: Standardize on /locations/{state}/{city}/ for all seven locations with 301s from old URLs.

findings.title: No IndexNow implementation detected
findings.description: No IndexNow key file found at /indexnow.txt or /.well-known/indexnow.txt.
findings.recommendation: Install an IndexNow-compatible plugin so new/updated content is pushed to Bing/Yandex immediately.

findings.title: Thin /locations/ and /services/ hub pages
findings.description: Both hub pages extract to under 75 words of unique body copy beyond the navigational card grid.
findings.recommendation: Add 150–300 words of unique summary copy to each hub page.

categories.name: Content Quality
what_works: Genuine, specific, AI-citation-ready numeric claims (cost ranges, lifespans) on several pages
Clean FAQ Q&A structure on /faq/, homepage, and /brooklyn-roofing-lp/
Legitimate external citations (U.S. DOE, Remodeling Magazine) in at least one blog post
Real, named customer testimonials (Sarah T., Dr. Louis Vastola, Chris W.)
Solid schema foundation: Organization, BlogPosting with author/dates, BreadcrumbList
Local specificity (neighborhoods, ZIP codes) on the Brooklyn pages

findings.title: Three separate URLs compete for the same "Brooklyn roofing" intent
findings.description: /locations/brooklyn-ny/, /brooklyn-roofing-lp/, and /affordable-roofing-in-brooklyn-ny/ repeat the same claims and near-identical 8-question FAQ blocks — a classic doorway-page pattern.
findings.recommendation: Pick one canonical Brooklyn page, 301 the other two, fold any unique content in as new sections.

findings.title: Duplicate "Old Bridge, NJ" pages with an inconsistent phone number
findings.description: /locations/new-jersey/old-bridge/ shows two different phone numbers on the same page ((848) 310-3977 and (347) 323-9128) while also overlapping /roofer-old-bridge-nj/.
findings.recommendation: Consolidate into one URL and standardize on a single phone number per NAP best practice.

findings.title: No visible author identity, credentials, or license number anywhere on the site
findings.description: Blog author ("Lonnie from ProLine Roofing") exists only in invisible schema; the FAQ says a license is "available upon request" rather than displaying the number.
findings.recommendation: Add visible bylines/bios, a Team/About page, and display the actual NY/NJ contractor license number in the footer.

findings.title: Orphan "asphalt shingle" landing page duplicates the official service page
findings.description: /asphalt-shingle-roofing-staten-island/ and /services/residential-roofing/asphalt-shingle-roofing/ target the same keyword with no cross-linking.
findings.recommendation: Treat the orphan page as a linked buyer's guide or merge and redirect.

findings.title: Core service pages fall well short of the 800-word floor
findings.description: /services/, /services/residential-roofing/, /services/commercial-roofing/, /services/gutter-services/ range 230–560 words of largely generic copy vs. /services/roof-repair/'s 1,320 words.
findings.recommendation: Bring all service pages up to the depth level of /services/roof-repair/ with material specs, process steps, and cost ranges.

findings.title: Boilerplate trust badges and testimonials copy-pasted verbatim across nearly every page
findings.description: The same 3 testimonials and "Accredited Company" badge (no accrediting body ever named) recur across home, services, and location pages.
findings.recommendation: Vary testimonials per location and name the actual accreditation or remove the badge.

findings.title: Homepage contains a duplicated "About Us" block within a single page
findings.description: Two near-identical About Us paragraphs appear back-to-back, plus an unrendered "Roofing Projects 0 +" stat counter.
findings.recommendation: Remove the duplicate block and verify the counter renders for non-JS/crawler contexts.

findings.title: Readability sits at college level (grade 11–13) on core pages
findings.description: Homepage and blog posts measure grade 11.4–13.4 vs. the ~8th–9th grade level recommended for consumer home-services content.
findings.recommendation: Shorten sentences; use the FAQ/brooklyn-roofing-lp writing style as the house style.

categories.name: Schema & Structured Data
what_works: JSON-LD used exclusively and @context is consistently correct
RoofingContractor + Organization is the correct, non-deprecated type where present
BreadcrumbList implemented site-wide with correct structure
WebSite + SearchAction correctly formed on the homepage
Dates in valid ISO 8601 format; no deprecated schema types found

findings.title: Sitewide Product + AggregateRating schema is misapplied and identically duplicated on every URL
findings.description: The exact same 4.9/97 rating is stamped on every page including blog and FAQ, disconnected from the real business entity — the textbook signature of spam/structured-data enforcement action.
findings.recommendation: Remove the block entirely; attach a real AggregateRating directly to the RoofingContractor entity, only on contextually appropriate pages.

findings.title: RoofingContractor/Organization NAP is invalid — no real street address
findings.description: streetAddress is literally "ProLine Roofing" instead of a real address on the homepage, /contact/, and /locations/brooklyn-ny/.
findings.recommendation: Supply the real address matching the Google Business Profile, or omit streetAddress and rely on areaServed if the address is intentionally unpublished.

findings.title: No areaServed anywhere despite the explicit 8-town service area
findings.description: The property Google recommends for Local Service Area Businesses is absent from every RoofingContractor block found.
findings.recommendation: Add an areaServed array to the main Organization node and a per-location areaServed on each location page.

findings.title: Duplicate/conflicting RoofingContractor entity on /locations/brooklyn-ny/ with a property typo
findings.description: A second, disconnected RoofingContractor node has a real address, a telePhone typo, and inconsistent openingHours formatting — creates entity ambiguity.
findings.recommendation: Fix the typo, confirm whether the Brooklyn address is real/staffed, and link via @id/parentOrganization rather than duplicating the entity.

findings.title: No Service schema on any of the 20+ /services/ pages
findings.description: Sampled service pages carry only BreadcrumbList and the spammy Product block — no Service/provider/areaServed markup at all.
findings.recommendation: Add a Service node per service page linked to the Organization @id as provider, with serviceType and areaServed.

findings.title: FAQPage schema absent on /faq/
findings.description: No SERP rich-result loss (Google retired FAQ rich results), but it's a missed AI/GEO citation opportunity for genuine business-authored Q&A.
findings.recommendation: Add FAQPage markup using the exact on-page Q&A copy.

findings.title: No Review/AggregateRating tied to real testimonials
findings.description: A ratings badge image implies third-party scores, but no legitimate Review/AggregateRating schema exists beyond the disconnected fake Product block.
findings.recommendation: Mark up individual Review objects against the RoofingContractor @id and roll into one accurate AggregateRating.

categories.name: Sitemap Architecture
what_works: All 5 sitemap files valid, well-formed XML
All 74 sitemap URLs return HTTP 200 with zero redirects
Well under the 50,000 URL per-file limit; sitemap index correctly used even at this scale
No deprecated priority/changefreq tags present
lastmod timestamps are realistic and track real edit history
category-sitemap.xml matches the live taxonomy 5/5
Location-page volume (~9–12 URLs) is far below doorway-page-risk thresholds

findings.title: Duplicate/competing location landing pages cannibalize the canonical location pages
findings.description: Brooklyn has 3 competing sitemapped pages, Old Bridge has 2, and NJ-overall has 2 — all self-canonicalized, none deferring to the "real" page.
findings.recommendation: Pick one canonical URL per location; redirect or noindex+exclude-from-sitemap the rest.

findings.title: Home-base location page (/locations/staten-island-ny/) missing from the sitemap with a conflicting canonical
findings.description: The page is live, nav-linked, and indexable, but canonicalizes to the homepage and is absent from page-sitemap.xml — an inconsistent signal.
findings.recommendation: Either redirect it to the homepage and remove the nav link, or self-canonicalize it, differentiate its content, and add it to the sitemap.

findings.title: local-sitemap.xml is a single-entity KML file, not a location-page index
findings.description: It contains one Placemark for the Staten Island HQ only — there is no structured geo/local signal for the 7 secondary towns via that channel.
findings.recommendation: Confirm each town location page carries its own LocalBusiness/areaServed schema separately; consider a multi-location plugin/GBP location group.

findings.title: /locations.kml sitemap entry may confuse sitemap consumers
findings.description: A KML geo file is listed as a regular sitemap <url> entry — valid per Rank Math design but easy to mistake for a broken URL on manual review.
findings.recommendation: No action required; document for future audits.

categories.name: Performance (Core Web Vitals)
what_works: LiteSpeed full-page cache active and hitting, with gzip enabled
Non-render-blocking CSS delivery via preload+onload swap pattern
JS combined/minified and mostly deferred
preload_check.py scored the homepage 100/100 (speculation rules, fetchpriority, preload hints, no bfcache killers)
Sane 7-day cache-control headers on static assets

findings.title: Render-blocking jQuery core script on every page
findings.description: jquery.min.js (87.5KB) loads with no async/defer on the homepage and all sampled inner pages — the one consistently render-blocking script found sitewide.
findings.recommendation: Enable LiteSpeed's defer/remote-load option for core jQuery, or use WP 6.3+ script loading strategies.

findings.title: LCP-candidate hero image lazy-loaded via JS swap despite fetchpriority="high"
findings.description: The real image URL only exists in data-src, requiring lazy-load JS to run before the browser can discover it — defeats the preload hint entirely.
findings.recommendation: Exclude the true LCP image from LiteSpeed's lazy-load feature and keep the real src/srcset inline.

findings.title: Oversized inline "critical CSS" block (87KB)
findings.description: LiteSpeed's auto-generated critical CSS is capturing near-full-page CSS rather than a true above-the-fold subset.
findings.recommendation: Regenerate Critical CSS scoped tighter to the actual above-the-fold viewport per template.

findings.title: Homepage images mostly missing intrinsic width/height
findings.description: 30 of 40 homepage tags rely on CSS sizing rather than width/height attributes — a CLS risk, especially versus the better-behaved location pages.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit width/height or aspect-ratio to every homepage image.

findings.title: Low adoption of modern image formats (WebP/AVIF)
findings.description: Only ~2 image references sitewide use WebP/AVIF; the bulk of content images are legacy JPG/PNG.
findings.recommendation: Enable automatic WebP/AVIF generation with picture-element fallback.

findings.title: Unverified third-party embed cost (YouTube iframe, Trustindex reviews widget)
findings.description: Common INP/main-thread offenders present on multiple pages; actual cost could not be measured in this sandbox.
findings.recommendation: Use a lightweight facade for the YouTube embed and verify Trustindex's main-thread cost with a real Lighthouse trace.

findings.title: No CrUX field data or working lab tooling available in this environment
findings.description: No Google API credentials configured, and Chromium could not complete a TLS handshake to the live site through the sandbox proxy — all performance findings are static/structural estimates, not measured LCP/INP/CLS.
findings.recommendation: Re-run this category with a configured GOOGLE_API_KEY or from an environment with working Chrome/Lighthouse access.

categories.name: Visual & Mobile
what_works: Correct responsive viewport meta tag on all pages checked
Phone number and "FREE ESTIMATE" CTA present in the global nav on every page (structurally above the fold)
Exactly one H1 per page with correct heading structure
Hero/logo images carry explicit width/height and low-weight placeholder patterns for CLS avoidance
No lorem ipsum or broken shortcode placeholders found

findings.title: Screenshots could not be captured — visual verification is incomplete
findings.description: Chromium/Playwright could not complete a TLS handshake to the live site through the sandbox's mandatory proxy (net::ERR_CONNECTION_RESET), even though plain HTTP fetches succeeded. No TLS-weakening workaround was attempted.
findings.recommendation: Re-run this category once browser access to the host is confirmed working through the proxy, or from an unproxied environment.

findings.title: Mobile hamburger menu toggle appears under the 48x48px touch-target guideline
findings.description: CSS custom properties suggest an estimated ~30x30px clickable area for the primary mobile nav control.
findings.recommendation: Increase the effective tap area to at least 44x44px via additional padding.

findings.title: Placeholder-style construction emoji in a location page H1
findings.description: "Roof Repair Staten Island 🚧" reads as unpolished for a professional roofing contractor.
findings.recommendation: Remove the emoji unless it's a deliberate, tested brand choice.

findings.title: Location page <title> typo ("Saten Island")
findings.description: User-visible in the browser tab and search snippets, affecting perceived polish and trust.
findings.recommendation: Fix to "Staten Island" and check other location pages for the same template typo.

categories.name: AI Search Readiness (GEO)
what_works: All sampled pages are server-rendered (no SPA/JS-gating) — fully accessible to non-JS AI crawlers
robots.txt does not block any AI crawler
BlogPosting schema with dates and a named author present on every post
Organization schema includes a broad sameAs set (Facebook, X, LinkedIn, Pinterest, YouTube, GBP)
Proper H1→H2→H3 heading hierarchy on blog posts
Specific, factual, locally-relevant statistics present as good raw citation material
One post already uses a "TL;DR" summary block — a template worth rolling out site-wide

findings.title: FAQ page has no FAQPage schema and questions aren't marked up as headings
findings.description: The 6 Q&A pairs on /faq/ are wrapped in decorative spans/divs, not h2/h3 tags, and there is no FAQPage JSON-LD — the weakest structural markup of any sampled page despite being the most AI-citation-ready content type.
findings.recommendation: Add FAQPage schema and convert questions into real headings; expand thin answers to include actual numbers.

findings.title: No llms.txt file
findings.description: https://www.proline-roofing.com/llms.txt returns 404 — no structured AI-crawler-facing manifest of the business, service areas, or key pages.
findings.recommendation: Publish an /llms.txt summarizing the business, service area, and top pages in Markdown link format.

findings.title: Blog content is fragmented into sub-134-word paragraphs with no self-contained answer blocks
findings.description: Sampled posts average 20–65 words per paragraph, well under the 134–167 word range shown to correlate with AI citation.
findings.recommendation: Add a consolidated 120–170 word answer paragraph under each H2/H3; roll out the existing TL;DR pattern site-wide.

findings.title: Headings are declarative, not question-phrased
findings.description: H2s like "5 Factors Affecting Roof Lifespan" don't match natural-language queries typed into ChatGPT/Perplexity/AI Overviews.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite H2/H3 headings as questions where natural, with a direct-answer sentence immediately below.

findings.title: Zero outbound citations to authoritative third-party sources
findings.description: Every statistic across 5 sampled pages is asserted with no attribution — Perplexity in particular favors sourced content.
findings.recommendation: Add 2–4 outbound citations per long-form post to manufacturer, code, or climate-data sources.

findings.title: robots.txt is silent rather than explicit on AI crawlers
findings.description: No named directives exist for GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, etc. — access is allowed only by default.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit Allow blocks for major AI crawlers to signal intentional AI-search visibility.

findings.title: No comparison/data tables for highly citable facts
findings.description: Cost-by-material and lifespan-by-material data is presented only as prose despite being inherently tabular.
findings.recommendation: Convert these sections into simple HTML tables — disproportionately picked up by AI Overviews and Perplexity.

categories.name: Local SEO
what_works: Dedicated, human-written location pages exist for every stated target market (Staten Island, Brooklyn, 6 NJ towns)
Genuine, live third-party review integration (Trustindex, 4.9★/97 reviews) with healthy recency
Visible NAP on the homepage/contact footer is internally consistent with itself
Main navigation correctly links to all location pages, including the Staten Island hub
aggregateRating present in structured data sitewide (though type-misapplied)

findings.title: Staten Island hub page canonical points to the homepage and is missing from the sitemap
findings.description: The primary market's own ~2,800-word location page shares only ~12% text similarity with the homepage yet is told to consolidate into it — blocking it from ranking independently.
findings.recommendation: Self-canonicalize /locations/staten-island-ny/ and add it to the XML sitemap.

findings.title: Sitewide RoofingContractor schema streetAddress bug
findings.description: streetAddress contains the business name instead of the real address (481 Mill Rd) on every page carrying that block.
findings.recommendation: Fix the field to the real, GBP-matching address.

findings.title: Brooklyn and Freehold page-level schema assert addresses never shown in visible content
findings.description: 225 Joralemon St (Brooklyn) and 144 Tilton Dr (Freehold) appear nowhere in the footer, contact page, or map embeds — the classic pattern of an undisclosed secondary-location listing, a real GBP policy risk.
findings.recommendation: Confirm whether these are genuine staffed locations; if not, remove them and rely on areaServed instead.

findings.title: Only 2 of 8 location pages carry any LocalBusiness schema at all
findings.description: Clifton, Elizabeth, Jersey City, Newark, Old Bridge, and both Staten Island pages have no LocalBusiness/areaServed/geo markup — only BreadcrumbList and the generic fake-review block.
findings.recommendation: Apply one consistent LocalBusiness + areaServed + geo template to every location page.

findings.title: Orphan landing pages create local-SEO cannibalization / duplicate-NAP risk
findings.description: Four of the five orphan pages directly duplicate a proper /locations/ page for the same city, splitting ranking signals and review/engagement equity.
findings.recommendation: Consolidate via 301 redirect or noindex + clear internal linking as PPC-only pages.

findings.title: NJ town pages are only ~19–33% unique content after normalizing town names
findings.description: Roughly two-thirds to four-fifths of each NJ town page's body text is shared templated boilerplate.
findings.recommendation: Add materially more town-specific detail: local landmarks, permit/code notes, project photos, local testimonials.

findings.title: Location pages use generic city-level Google Maps embeds, not a verified GBP pin
findings.description: Every location page embeds a generic maps.google.com city-level query rather than a real business pin.
findings.recommendation: Replace with a real GBP place embed where a verified presence exists, or drop the map in favor of a clear service-area statement.

categories.name: Search Experience Optimization (SXO)
what_works: /locations/brooklyn-ny/ proves the CMS/theme can produce a fully SERP-aligned Local Page (schema, depth, testimonials all present)
A shared testimonial/trust widget gives a consistent social-proof baseline across core pages
Click-to-call and "free estimate" CTAs present almost everywhere checked
The /locations/ hub architecture structurally matches what Google rewards for these queries
Active content maintenance evidenced by recent 2025–2026 publish/update dates

findings.title: Three pages carry BlogPosting schema for transactional local-service queries
findings.description: roof-replacement-in-staten-island-made-easy, affordable-roofing-in-brooklyn-ny, and asphalt-shingle-roofing-staten-island are tagged as blog articles despite targeting local commercial intent where every SERP competitor is a Local/Service page — the single most severe page-type mismatch found.
findings.recommendation: Re-tag with Service/RoofingContractor schema or fold content into the matching /services/ or /locations/ page.

findings.title: Sitewide absence of LocalBusiness/RoofingContractor schema (only 1 of 16 pages checked has it)
findings.description: Only /locations/brooklyn-ny/ has full schema; no page anywhere has AggregateRating/Review schema despite visible testimonial content.
findings.recommendation: Roll out the Brooklyn schema template sitewide and add Review schema wherever testimonials appear.

findings.title: Commercial roofing page fails the NJ property-manager persona (31/100)
findings.description: 574 words, no case studies/portfolio/bonding credentials, and one H2 literally reads "Persistent Leaks Ruining Your Home?" on a B2B page — the weakest persona score in the audit.
findings.recommendation: Build a dedicated commercial + NJ hybrid page with case studies, bonding/insurance badges, and warranty-term callouts.

findings.title: Gutter installation page is ~7x thinner than the SERP norm with zero location targeting
findings.description: 518 words / 4 H2s vs. the leading local competitor's 3,778 words / 23 H2s of location-specific proof.
findings.recommendation: Expand to a full local-service page with pricing, materials, process, and Staten Island/NJ town mentions.

findings.title: Brooklyn query cluster is cannibalized across three internal pages
findings.description: Inconsistent schema and trust-signal depth across the three competing Brooklyn URLs splits authority instead of concentrating it.
findings.recommendation: Consolidate the two orphan Brooklyn pages into /locations/brooklyn-ny/, porting over the strongest conversion copy.

findings.title: No GAF/BBB/manufacturer certification badges found on any page
findings.description: Every ranking competitor across all 5 query clusters leads with certification/warranty proof; no such badge appears anywhere on the site.
findings.recommendation: Surface any held manufacturer certifications prominently with badge + schema on all service/location pages.

findings.title: Title tag typo damages trust at the highest-intent emergency-repair moment
findings.description: "Roof Repair Saten Island, NY" is visible directly in the SERP snippet for an emergency-repair query.
findings.recommendation: Fix the typo — a one-line change with outsized trust impact.

categories.name: Content Clustering & Strategy
what_works: A 5-category taxonomy maps reasonably well to funnel stages
Several posts already carry genuine in-body contextual links to sibling posts
roof-replacement-in-staten-island-made-easy (refreshed July 2026) is a strong pillar candidate
The repairs-problem-solving category is the most complete, cluster-ready topical grouping
Service/location URL hierarchies already exist, so hub-and-spoke destination pages are already built

findings.title: No true pillar pages exist — category archives are being used as false hubs
findings.description: No post is structured as a comprehensive 2,500+ word guide; the closest candidates are cross-tagged into 3–4 categories simultaneously, signaling no fixed ownership per topic.
findings.recommendation: Build two pillars (Roof Replacement Guide, Roofing Costs Guide) to 2,500–4,000 words each with a TOC and dedicated schema.

findings.title: 13 of 19 posts (68%) are not reachable from the main /blog/ index
findings.description: /blog/ hard-caps at 6 posts with no pagination — the rest are only discoverable via category archives or the sitemap.
findings.recommendation: Add pagination or restructure /blog/ into a curated hub grouped by pillar cluster.

findings.title: Blog-to-service links are template navigation, not contextual hub-spoke CTAs
findings.description: Every post carries the identical 25-link services mega-menu rather than hand-picked, topically-matched in-paragraph links to a specific service subpage.
findings.recommendation: Add one or two hand-picked, keyword-anchored contextual links per post to the single most relevant service page.

findings.title: One post is orphaned from the category system and the blog index entirely
findings.description: 5-types-of-roofing-you-should-consider appears on no category archive and isn't among the 6 posts shown on /blog/.
findings.recommendation: Assign it to roofing-101 and include it in the Materials cluster.

findings.title: Major content gaps versus a full local roofing content strategy
findings.description: No insurance-claims guide, no warranty comparisons, no non-winter seasonal content, zero commercial-roofing or gutter blog support, and no NJ-town-specific posts despite 6 NJ location pages.
findings.recommendation: Prioritize an insurance-claims guide, a warranty-comparison guide, NJ-town posts for top markets, and small commercial/gutter mini-clusters.

findings.title: Cannibalization risk from cost-related post overlap
findings.description: roofing-costs-decoded and the-real-cost-of-roof-repairs-in-staten-island target overlapping cost-intent queries with no clear pillar/spoke split.
findings.recommendation: Designate roofing-costs-decoded as the pillar and narrow the other into a repair-cost-specific spoke.

categories.name: Backlinks & Domain Authority
what_works: Domain is present in the Common Crawl web graph and clears the ranking-inclusion threshold
No spam/toxic-pattern signals found in any data source checked
Outbound social citations (Facebook, LinkedIn, X, Pinterest) are consistent, real business profiles
No reciprocal-link scheme risk beyond the expected owned-profile pattern

findings.title: Referring-domain count, Domain Authority, and Spam Score are completely unmeasured at this data tier
findings.description: Only Common Crawl + verification crawler are available (no Moz/Bing keys); Common Crawl's sample surfaced zero referring domains for this site — not evidence of zero backlinks, just no usable data at this tier.
findings.recommendation: Sign up for the free Moz API tier (2,500 rows/month, no cost) to unlock DA/PA, referring-domain counts, and spam score.

findings.title: Domain registration heritage could not be verified
findings.description: WHOIS lookup timed out in this sandbox (TCP/43 egress restricted) — registration age/expired-domain-abuse risk is UNKNOWN, not confirmed clean.
findings.recommendation: Re-run domain history from an unrestricted network path, or pull registration data via a registrar-facing RDAP/WHOIS web lookup.

findings.title: Only 4 inbound-link candidates identified, all owned-profile citations
findings.description: Verification was limited to the site's own outbound social links; this says nothing about genuine third-party referring-domain size or quality.
findings.recommendation: Treat this as a NAP-hygiene check only, not a backlink-authority assessment, until Tier 1/2 data sources are enabled.

phases.name: Phase 1: Critical Fixes
items: Remove the sitewide fake Product/AggregateRating (4.9★/97) schema block from every page and move a real AggregateRating onto the RoofingContractor entity (Schema, Technical)
Fix the RoofingContractor streetAddress field — replace "ProLine Roofing" with the real street address (Schema, Local)
Investigate and resolve the undisclosed Brooklyn (225 Joralemon St) and Freehold (144 Tilton Dr) schema addresses — remove if not genuine staffed/GBP locations (Local, Schema)
Self-canonicalize /locations/staten-island-ny/ (remove the homepage canonical) and add it to the XML sitemap (Local, Sitemap, Technical)
Resolve the 5 orphan PPC landing pages: noindex+canonical-to-real-page or 301 redirect, and remove from sitemaps (Technical, Sitemap, Content, Local, SXO)
Re-tag the 3 pages carrying BlogPosting schema on transactional local queries with Service/RoofingContractor schema (SXO, Schema)

phases.name: Phase 2: High-Impact Improvements
items: Add security response headers (HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, CSP, X-Frame-Options) via LiteSpeed/.htaccess (Technical)
Roll out consistent LocalBusiness/RoofingContractor + areaServed + geo schema to every location page using the Brooklyn page as the template (Schema, Local, SXO)
Add Service schema to all /services/ pages (Schema, SXO)
Build a dedicated commercial-roofing + NJ hybrid page with case studies, bonding/insurance badges, and warranty terms (SXO, Content)
Fix the render-blocking jQuery script and the lazy-loaded LCP hero image (Performance)
Consolidate the Brooklyn and Old Bridge duplicate/cannibalizing pages into single authoritative pages (Content, Local, SXO, Sitemap)
Add visible author bylines/bios and display the actual contractor license number in the footer (Content, GEO)
Fix the "Saten Island" title typo and the telePhone schema typo (Visual, SXO, Schema)

phases.name: Phase 3: Content & Authority
items: Expand thin core service pages (/services/, /services/residential-roofing/, /services/commercial-roofing/, /services/gutter-services/) to 800+ words with material specs, process, and cost ranges (Content)
Expand NJ town location pages beyond ~19-33% unique content with local landmarks, permit notes, and photos (Local)
Add FAQPage schema and convert /faq/ accordion questions into real headings; expand thin answers (Schema, GEO)
Publish an /llms.txt file and add explicit AI-crawler Allow directives in robots.txt (GEO)
Build two content pillars (Roof Replacement Guide, Roofing Costs Guide) and restructure /blog/ so all 19 posts are reachable (Cluster)
Add contextual, hand-picked internal links from blog posts to specific service subpages (Cluster, SXO)
Add outbound citations and cost/lifespan comparison tables to blog content (GEO, Content)
Sign up for the free Moz API and Bing Webmaster Tools to unlock real backlink/DA data (Backlinks)

phases.name: Phase 4: Monitoring & Iteration
items: Re-run PageSpeed Insights/Lighthouse and pull CrUX field data once Google API credentials are configured (Performance)
Capture desktop/mobile screenshots once browser access to the site is confirmed working, to complete the visual QA pass (Visual)
Verify GBP primary category and confirm no duplicate/unverified GBP listings exist for the Brooklyn/Freehold addresses (Local)
Establish a quarterly content-review cadence with genuine refreshes, not cosmetic timestamp bumps (GEO, Content)
Manually verify Tier-1 citation presence (Yelp, BBB, Angi, Thumbtack) against the corrected canonical NAP (Local, Backlinks)
Monitor review velocity and institute an owner-response cadence on Google reviews (Local)
